tests.message: The concurrency tests rely on a hard-coded `time.sleep(0.05)` in the mocked `urlopen` to widen the race window; on extremely slow or heavily loaded systems this may not be sufficient to deterministically reproduce the race, making the tests potentially flaky.

No test exercises the case where `_get_jwt()` raises an exception (e.g., token-exchange failure) under concurrent access; the lock's behavior on exception propagation to other waiting threads is not verified.
The concurrency tests use only 10 threads, but the motivating scenario (`linked_sources` prewarm ThreadPoolExecutor) may produce higher contention; a higher-thread-count variant is not covered.

PR body and issue #581 acceptance criteria require pinning PyGithub (or replacing the import); no requirements.txt diff is present in the corpus, so the dependency upgrade cannot be verified and the production ImportError branch cannot be confirmed closed.

PR claims tests pinning the fail-closed behavior of _resolve_maintainers; the diff instead adds TestJwtCacheConcurrency to tests/test_forgejo_backend.py, so the issue #581 acceptance criterion ("A test pins the fail-closed behavior") is not demonstrable from the supplied diff.

Diff/PR mismatch: PR is classified dependency_upgrade and titled as a precheck.py fail-closed fix, but the actual code change is a thread-safety refactor of the Forgejo JWT cache; the title/body/classification/linked-issue must be reconciled before merge.

TestJwtCacheConcurrency never exercises the urlopen-raises path; the suite asserts nothing about exception propagation or cache state when the underlying fetch fails, leaving the PR's own "fail closed on errors" theme untested for the JWT cache.
_run_concurrent_get_jwt widens the race window with a hardcoded time.sleep(0.05); on a heavily loaded CI runner the window can collapse and the assertion can pass for the wrong reason.
After the concurrent burst the tests assert only the returned tokens and urlopen.call_count, never verifying fb._JWT_CACHE / fb._JWT_CACHE_TIME were correctly populated by the single surviving fetch.

correctness.message: PR title/body reference a precheck.py fail-closed permission-check fix (issue #581) and the metadata lists precheck.py/requirements.txt as changed files, but the diff only adds thread-safety (RLock) for the JWT cache in forgejo_backend.py and a TestJwtCacheConcurrency class; either the diff is truncated or the title/body/classification is mislabeled — flag for the main reviewer to confirm scope before merge.

tests.message: TestJwtCacheConcurrency never exercises the concurrent-fetch-error path: when urlopen raises, no assertion covers whether the exception propagates to all threads and whether _JWT_CACHE/_JWT_CACHE_TIME remain unset (the fail-closed behavior that the PR's stated theme — fail closed on errors — would actually require testing).

_run_concurrent_get_jwt relies on a hard-coded time.sleep(0.05) inside the mocked urlopen to widen the race window; under a heavily loaded CI runner the 10-thread burst could still collapse the window and skip the gap the test exists to catch, making the assertion mock_urlopen.call_count == 1 timing-sensitive.

After the concurrent burst the tests only assert returned values and call_count; they never verify fb._JWT_CACHE and fb._JWT_CACHE_TIME are the value/timestamp from the single fetch, so a bug that returned the right token but left the cache stale/empty would go undetected.

PR metadata names pr_reviewer/precheck.py and tests/test_precheck.py as the changed files and describes pinning PyGithub / empty-set fail-closed for issue #581, but the diff shown modifies pr_reviewer/forgejo_backend.py and tests/test_forgejo_backend.py for JWT-cache concurrency (#538); the review corpus cannot be matched to test coverage for the described change.
